notes: Connected OSM course candidate. The selected loop is the longest simple source-node cycle after explicit exclusions; its association with a named circuit configuration requires review.
Source way order and shared node IDs are retained. No nearby endpoints are joined and no reference boundaries are read.
Some source ways lack one-way direction tags. Travel direction is provisional.

source.name: Mapzen Terrain Tiles
attribution: Global elevation data courtesy of the U.S. Geological Survey and NOAA.

sources.notes: Road elevations are edited from Geospatial Information Authority of Japan (GSI) DEM5A ground tiles. Edited from GSI elevation tiles: bilinear ground samples outside the declared crossing intervals, compressed within 0.25 m of those samples. Both the upper deck and occluded lower road interpolate between their separate sampled approach endpoints. Interior raster cells are excluded from both spans, so deck heights cannot raise the lower road. Heights and separation remain estimates, not a bridge survey; no nominal height is assigned. No capture date is supplied by these tile responses. The bridge uses explicit paired source stations; cross-sections never select another road branch. Curbs are geometry-based illustrations, not verified curb locations. Banking is unknown and assumed zero. Borders retain their feature licences and unverified status. Imagery loads externally; no meshes, image bytes or videos are stored.

supersedes.reason: Correct the flattened overpass with image-reviewed paired road limits and separate ground-approach heights, preserving the original trace, timing and border/model proof.

measurement.note: Road-edge estimates from the pinned licensed satellite image. Seventy labelled cross-section controls constrain visible pavement transitions, read with roughly one metre precision; this is not surveyed positional accuracy. The left pit-opening edge near station285 and hidden lower road near station795 use estimated joins between visible adjacent limits. Dense fitted controls sample linear normal-offset interpolation along the retained source path; they are not additional independent image observations. No nominal road width or reference-length fit is used. Curbs remain illustrative, banking unknown and road heights estimated from ground approaches.

crossings.note: Pinned OSM bridge segment. The upper interval includes both mapped deck endpoints and adjoining approach samples; the lower interval identifies the separately mapped road. Heights are edited from GSI DEM5A ground samples, not a surveyed clearance.

elevation.note: Edited from GSI elevation tiles: bilinear ground samples outside the declared crossing intervals, compressed within 0.25 m of those samples. Both the upper deck and occluded lower road interpolate between their separate sampled approach endpoints. Interior raster cells are excluded from both spans, so deck heights cannot raise the lower road. Heights and separation remain estimates, not a bridge survey; no nominal height is assigned. No capture date is supplied by these tile responses.

borderInference.note: Road-border estimates reconstructed from complete pairs of sparse image-edge measurements. Each pair defines its own road section; the original trace is preserved and constrains station displacement and route order. Linear intervals, junction openings and curbs remain estimates, not surveyed racing limits. Every saved edge station and anchor requires pinned-image coverage during authoring. No automatic evidence scores are claimed.
